title: Manage projects
goal: The project has one handoff chain from scope to close: what it is for and how it will be judged, a plan with the roles and resources it needs, evidence as it runs, a report against its measures, and a closing record of what was learned.

steps.do: Write what the project must make true, what it will not do, the people, money and tools it needs, and the measures and indicators it will be judged by, and bring the founder the case for doing it now against the other work in flight, since choosing and funding a project is the founder's.

Pick how this project will be run from how uncertain its outcome is, a short fixed sequence when the work is known and a set of timeboxed attempts when it is not, and write the choice and its reason on the project's handoff.

Break the project into handoffs with done criteria in the order they must finish, name the role on each and the tools or access it needs, say who is told what as the work lands, and leave the hiring, the spending and the launch date to the founder.

Work the handoffs in order, write evidence against each done criterion as it passes, report the project's status with what moved and what is blocked, and bring any change to its scope back to the founder rather than absorbing it.

Report the project against the measures its scope named: what was delivered, what the measure now reads, how long each stage took and where the time went, each cited to a handoff or an evidence record.
Close the project's handoffs, write the recurring work it leaves behind as a process record with an owner, and record what would be done differently next time as lessons another project can reuse.
Raise to the strategy lead whether the project met what it was started for, and what the venture should do with the capability it now has.

done_criteria.check: Is the project reported against the measures its own scope named, and does its close leave an owned process record for the recurring work it created?
